headline: A paper reports semantic stop-token alignment reduces length inflation in on-policy distillation
summary: A September 17 preprint studies length inflation in sampled-token on-policy distillation (OPD). It argues that when a base student and post-trained teacher encode the same stopping decision with different tokens, the teacher can give a negative signal to the student’s sampled EOS while the teacher-preferred token receives little support. Across Qwen3, Llama 3.2 and Gemma 3, the authors report that aligning total probability over semantically equivalent stop tokens in the distillation signal reduces mismatch-driven length and clipping; merely expanding the decoder stop set does not. An earlier OPD paper already describes EOS canonicalization in Appendix D, so the basic alignment idea is prior art; the newer paper adds cross-family empirical comparisons, a shared-declared-set Gemma test and stage-wise residual analysis. It also reports late-stage K2-Horizon re-inflation after correction. These are author-run, single-turn mathematical-reasoning results; multi-turn/tool semantics and independent replication remain open.
